_comment: Shared defaults. Your own budgets and limits go in settings.local.json (the Settings screen writes there; it is gitignored). account.label is auto-detected from ~/.claude.json. Account, billing period, plan limits and budgets. Anything set to null is reported by the dashboard as 'Unavailable from connected Claude data' rather than being invented.

limits._comment: Set these ONLY from your real plan. null => dashboard shows the metric as unavailable instead of guessing.

budgets._comment: Set your real budgets here. null => the dashboard reports 'No budget configured' instead of scoring you against an invented number.

waste_rules._low_output_note: Sessions are flagged when their output/billable ratio falls below this fraction of YOUR median session ratio, rather than an absolute number, because a healthy ratio depends on how agentic your workload is.

hygiene._comment: Context sizes (prompt-side tokens) the hygiene view reports spend above. Observed shares only; no saving is estimated from them.

anomaly._comment: session_ratio is measured against the MEDIAN session, not the mean: session sizes are right-skewed enough that a mean lets the outliers inflate their own baseline. Session token counts are heavy-tailed, so max_session_outliers, not the ratio, is what keeps the list short and leaves room for the other anomaly types. daily_robust_z is a threshold on a median/MAD robust z-score (MAD scaled by 1.4826 to estimate a stdev), not the plain daily_zscore: unpriced $0 days from agents with no pricing data would otherwise pollute a mean/stdev baseline.

scorecard._comment: The scorecard has no targets to configure: its three dimensions (Context share, Cache break-even, Budget adherence) are each measured directly from your transcripts, except budget adherence which needs a budget configured above.
